# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026 with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the Client Profile rather than from earlier Academy findings.

The Client's AI portfolio is at an early stage. A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal. AI visual inspection is being piloted on the German production line, and AI sales forecasting is planned for next year. The Client describes its AI maturity as Piloting.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists. Who owns the remediation of that finding is Unknown. The named regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. How either applies to each use case has not been established and should be determined by counsel.

The Client's incumbent frameworks are an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. Their scope, certification status and any associated records are Unknown. This proposal assumes no existing AI register, control or process until the Client confirms one.

The Client has stated three constraints. Customer data must stay in the EU. The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff. Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory

At Piloting maturity, governance decisions are being made in real time as systems move from pilot toward production. The stated objective is to have governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. Meeting that objective requires sustained attention across several areas at once:

* the AI inventory gap raised by internal audit
* the works council consultation
* EU data residency
* preparation for ISO/IEC 42001.

A single assessment would describe the gap but would not support the decisions that follow it. A fractional advisor gives the Sponsor a standing senior counterpart for those decisions. It does so without adding headcount, and the Client keeps ownership of every outcome.

The engagement applies three principles throughout: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice, every recommendation is framed for a named Client decision maker. Accountability for each decision stays with that person.

The working frameworks are:

* the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen).

Where executive or board reporting is needed, the engagement draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Annual Arc

The engagement start date is Unknown and depends on the decision expected by 15 December 2026. It is also Unknown whether Q2 2027 refers to a calendar or fiscal quarter. The arc below is sequenced so that visual inspection governance is completed in Quarter 1, which places it ahead of production. If commencement falls later than January 2027, Quarter 1 work will be compressed accordingly.

The ISO/IEC 42001 start date is not fixed and is rendered Unknown. Audit preparation intensity is therefore placed in Quarters 3 and 4 and will move once the date is confirmed.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.**
* Establish the AI system inventory in response to the June 2026 internal audit finding, using the GRC Workbook structure.
* Define roles and decision rights for AI governance. Current role assignments are Unknown and will be confirmed with the Sponsor.
* Prepare a governance pathway for the visual inspection pilot, including a documented works council consultation plan. The current state of that consultation is Unknown.
* Flag EU AI Act classification questions for each use case to counsel for verification.

**Quarter 2: Deepen.**
* Support the executive go or no-go decision on visual inspection production readiness.
* Review the deployed chatbot against the EU data residency constraint and GDPR considerations. The chatbot's hosting and data locations are Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.
* Introduce Slow AI Kitchen intake practices for new use cases.

**Quarter 3: Assure.**
* Conduct an ISO/IEC 42001 readiness gap assessment, mapped where useful to the existing ISMS and QMS once their scope is confirmed.
* Run a pre-deployment intake for AI sales forecasting. Its timing within next year is Unknown.
* Prepare evidence collection practices that the two internal auditors can test.

**Quarter 4: Evolve.**
* Consolidate readiness evidence toward ISO/IEC 42001.
* Hold the quarterly review of the year's progress.
* Set the governance agenda for the following year.
* Present renewal options in Month 11.

All ISO/IEC 42001 work is expressed as readiness. No certification or audit outcome is promised.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The engagement runs on four standing elements:

* **Monthly executive advisory session** with the Sponsor and executive attendees nominated by the Sponsor.
* **Monthly working session** with the governance team.
* **Asynchronous availability** for defined question categories, with response windows and escalation paths agreed in the first month.
* **Quarterly governance review.**

Attendance for each session is Unknown and will be set by the Sponsor. The roles available to participate include the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command.

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised in sessions are flagged for counsel verification and are not presented as settled advice.

## 6. Investment

The program is priced at **US$10,000 per month** for 12 months, renewable.

The approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The Client's fiscal year dates are Unknown, so how the engagement months fall across fiscal years cannot yet be confirmed. We ask the Sponsor to confirm fiscal year boundaries and budget availability for months that fall in the following fiscal year.
